subject: Payment path & vendor setup — pilot billing options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Claire Morgan <claire@cloudlinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T16:05:00-04:00
Subject: Payment path & vendor setup — pilot billing options

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the time. Quick post-call recap and three quick asks so we can lock in a smooth pilot: 

1) Pilot billing preference: will Cloudline prefer to run the pilot on corporate card (fastest) or start a vendor PO record? If the pilot is small ($5k-$15k) most customers do card for speed.

2) If you expect PO procurement for the pilot or production, can you share: AP lead time, any vendor-onboarding checklist (W-9, COI, security questionnaire), and approval thresholds (e.g., PO required > $50k)?

3) Marketplace interest: are you interested in Marketplace billing (AWS Marketplace) for procurement reasons, or would a standard Net30 invoice / card flow work? Marketplace adds an onboarding step but can simplify long-term contracting for some teams.

Attached is a short payment questionnaire (payment-questionnaire.pdf) you can fill or answer inline — it helps us produce a sample invoice and an estimated go-live date. Proposed next steps (feel free to adjust):
- You: confirm pilot payment path and procurement contact (AP/procurement email).
- Us: return a sample invoice, W-9, and security questionnaire; estimate lead times for PO onboarding vs card start.
- Schedule a 15-min check-in after AP confirms vendor requirements.

Would Tuesday 9/15 10:00am ET work for a quick call to align with AP?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
viv...@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: payment-questionnaire.pdf
From: Claire Morgan <claire@cloudlinehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudlinehealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T17:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Payment path & vendor setup — pilot billing options

Hi Vivek,

Thanks — quick answers to help you scope:
- AP policy: vendor PO required for spend > $50k.
- For smaller pilots (< $15k) we typically pay via corporate card to avoid vendor setup delays.
- Required vendor docs for a PO: W-9, payable remit information, completed security questionnaire (we run a short security intake). I attached our AP policy excerpt (CLH-APPolicy.pdf).

A couple of questions back to you:
1) Does Redwood support billing via AWS Marketplace (that would be preferred by our procurement team long-term)?
2) Can you share a sample invoice and clarify if Redwood supports Net30 terms on enterprise deals?

Procurement is on this thread (procurement@cloudlinehealth.com). If there are standard vendor documents you can pre-send (W-9, security questionnaire, sample invoice) that will speed things up.

I can confirm who from procurement will own the vendor record once I hear how you prefer to handle the pilot.

Best,
Claire Morgan
Head of Partnerships, Cloudline Health
claire@cloudlinehealth.com

Attachments: CLH-APPolicy.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T10:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Payment path & vendor setup — pilot billing options

On Sun, Sep 13, 2026 at 5:10 PM Claire Morgan <claire@cloudlinehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks — quick answers to help you scope:
> - AP policy: vendor PO required for spend > $50k.
> - For smaller pilots (< $15k) we typically pay via corporate card to avoid vendor setup delays.
> - Required vendor docs for a PO: W-9, payable remit information, completed security questionnaire (we run a short security intake). I attached our AP policy excerpt (CLH-APPolicy.pdf).

Thanks for the clarity — helpful. Short answers inline and attachments included:
- Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace in select regions. Marketplace billing is an option but it requires a separate onboarding and partner setup (typically 2–3 weeks). For a fast pilot, card or Net30 invoice is faster. See attached aws-marketplace-brief.pdf for details.
- Net30: yes, we can support Net30 invoicing for enterprise agreements; payment terms are part of the commercial SOW. We can do Net30 for the production contract; pilots are often card or upfront invoice.
- Vendor docs: attached redwood-w9.pdf and security-questionnaire-filled.pdf. Also attaching a redwood-invoice-sample.pdf so AP can see the remit fields we populate.

Proposed concrete next steps:
1) If you want the pilot on card, confirm the cardholder name and billing contact and we will provision the trial quickly (no vendor record required).
2) If you want PO for pilot, please confirm AP contact and expected lead time; we will put together a minimal PO acceptance packet to speed vendor onboarding.
3) Fill the short payment-questionnaire.pdf (or reply inline) so we can generate a sample invoice with your remit fields.

I set aside Tue 9/15 10:00am ET for a 15-minute alignment. If that works for procurement, please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
viv...@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-w9.pdf, security-questionnaire-filled.pdf, redwood-invoice-sample.pdf, aws-marketplace-brief.pdf, payment-questionnaire.pdf

Vivek —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. Procurement will try to put the pilot spend on the corporate card to avoid vendor setup delays. I asked AP to open a vendor record for Redwood for transitional/production usage; procurement lead for vendor setup is Tom Ellis (tom.ellis@cloudlinehealth.com).

We will:
- Fill and return the payment-questionnaire by EOD 2026-09-16.
- Confirm cardholder details for the pilot in a separate note.

The 9/15 10:00am ET slot should work as a short check-in — send a calendar invite and include Tom if possible. If procurement needs more time for PO onboarding we will follow up with an estimated vendor-creation date.

Thanks,
Claire
